input.question: When do LLM multi-agent systems fail to beat single agents, and what collective failure modes do they show?

supporting.quote: it confers systematic benefits specifically in long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies, while single-agent harnesses remain superior in tightly coupled, sequential workflows
supporting.why: Single agents win on tightly coupled sequential work.

supporting.quote: LLM populations were generally far more susceptible to herding behavior, and unlike humans, LLM cascades were less able to self-correct

draft_answer: Multi-agent setups help mainly on long-horizon tasks with sparse dependencies and lose to single agents on tightly coupled work; populations of LLM agents also herd and cascade without self-correcting.
